title: Shirakawa-go vs Takayama: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Takayama for substance and variety; Shirakawa-go for the iconic winter farmhouse scenery. Base in Takayama, day-trip to Shirakawa-go.

categories.name: Traditional Architecture
categories.summary: Shirakawa-go has the iconic UNESCO farmhouses; Takayama has Sanmachi Suji merchant quarter and Hida Folk Village.

categories.name: Food & Dining
categories.summary: Takayama has Hida beef, sake breweries, and morning markets. Shirakawa-go has very limited food options.

categories.name: Cost
categories.summary: Takayama delivers more per yen. Shirakawa-go adds ¥4,660 round-trip bus on top of entry fees.

categories.name: Transit
categories.summary: Takayama has JR train from Nagoya. Shirakawa-go is bus-only, requiring advance booking.

categories.name: Best Season
categories.summary: Shirakawa-go wins in winter. Takayama is excellent year-round.

categories.name: Time Needed
categories.summary: Shirakawa-go takes 2-4 hours. Takayama needs 2 full days.

categories.name: Accommodation
categories.summary: Takayama has broader range. Shirakawa-go minka is special but expensive.

categories.name: Crowds
categories.summary: Shirakawa-go gets overwhelmed with tour buses. Takayama absorbs crowds better.

faq.question: Should I visit Shirakawa-go or Takayama?
faq.answer: Takayama, and add Shirakawa-go as a day trip.

faq.question: How far is Shirakawa-go from Takayama?
faq.answer: 50 km, 50-60 min by Nohi Bus, ¥2,600 one-way.

faq.question: Is Shirakawa-go worth visiting?
faq.answer: Yes, especially in winter. Covers in 2-4 hours.
